answer: An agent buying ocean surveys of a jetty and a submerged ledge ranks providers by short random walks starting at its trusted contacts in a signed endorsement graph. Each walk gives one ticket to its endpoint; the buyer fixes the start distribution and walk length. Fake accounts can rearrange walks after entry into their cluster, but cannot increase the chance of entering it through unchanged honest endorsements. Their total ticket share is bounded by that entry probability. This works only when honest contacts rarely endorse sybils.
